fr_0019_evidence_for_orchestrator.request: fr-0019: Does the Resource Groups Tagging API GetResources operation return IAM roles?
fr_0019_evidence_for_orchestrator.finding: Probably no. The Resource Groups and Tag Editor resource table lists AWS::IAM::Role with 'Tag Editor Tagging: No' and 'Tag-based Groups: No' (only 'CloudFormation Stack-based Groups: Yes'), while AWS::IAM::ManagedPolicy, InstanceProfile and the other IAM types are Yes, with a footnote that they are global resources hosted in us-east-1.

evidence.note: The page is about Tag Editor and tag-based groups, not GetResources by name, so a registrar must decide whether it answers fr-0019. The page https://docs.aws.amazon.com/resourcegroupstagging/latest/APIReference/supported-services.html saved with no text.

fr_0019_evidence_for_orchestrator.effect: If IAM roles are not returned, the verify of iam-t02 and iam-t03 (resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters Key=task,Values=<id>) prints an empty list even when the role was not deleted: the verify cannot fail.
fr_0019_evidence_for_orchestrator.suggested_fix_needs_T108_exception: aws iam list-roles --query "Roles[?RoleName=='saa-iam-t03'].RoleName" expects an empty list and exits 0 after the cleanup (better than get-role, which exits non-zero with NoSuchEntity and would count as a failed command in tasks emulate). It does not filter by a tag, so T108 needs the exception named in exemplar/README.md.

emulate_not_run: tasks emulate is optional. Its rule 'a break-it step must fail' does not fit the simulator break steps of iam-t02 and iam-t03 (the command exits 0 and prints explicitDeny or implicitDeny), so an emulation would report fail and T114 would then block the tasks gate.
